claim: Running the Symmetrize operation (or a mirror-based workflow) on an object whose transforms haven't been applied (Ctrl+A: location/rotation) produces incorrect, broken symmetry -- the creator hit this directly, caught it, and corrected by applying transforms before symmetrizing.
supporting_evidence: Direct quote (5:23-5:47): "make sure you should apply your location and rotation before taking the symmetry that mistake i did here before then i realized i didn't apply the location and rotation so that's why you need to apply the low location and rotation on your mesh then you will be able to get the proper symmetry for your mesh" -- repeated again at 7:52-8:22: "the most important thing while applying the symmetry apply the location and rotation so you can see my origin should be in the at 3d cursor or at the center of the mesh and then you can get the right shape"

claim: To carve a boolean-style triangular cut into a mesh while keeping it as real topology (not a Boolean modifier): select the face(s) marking the intended cut region, Inset (I) to create a dedicated boundary ring, then select the outer edge of that boundary and Extrude+Scale it inward/along the surface normal to physically sink the cut into the mesh, rather than subtracting a separate cutter object.
supporting_evidence: Direct quote (0:43-1:00): "then press i to insert like this and you can see this face will be the boolean part so select the outer edge and extrude it and scale it and just maintain the scale from all sides same equals portion of scale"
